summary: Feed s076_single is degraded for IDS use: 50.9% of TCP sessions are one-way (54/106), violating the IDS requirement for bidirectional traffic. All other checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, drops, overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is delivering only one direction per flow to this IDS port. 54 of 106 TCP sessions show traffic in a single direction, indicating asymmetric capture - either only one side of the link is tapped/mirrored, or separate directional feeds are not aggregated, or load-balancing is splitting forward and reverse flows to different tool ports without bidirectional affinity.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP state tracking, stream reassembly and signature matching. With 50.9% one-way sessions the IDS cannot see handshakes, responses or return payloads, causing incomplete flow reconstruction, missed exploits/C2/exfiltration and high false-negative rate.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both forward and reverse directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port with bidirectional flow affinity to restore complete session visibility required for stateful IDS detection.
